wonder_status.wonder_list: Ancient Seven Wonders (honorary; only one still standing)

facts.text: The only surviving wonder of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
It was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for over 3800 years.
Built as a tomb for the Pharaoh Khufu during the Fourth Dynasty.
Estimated to be made of around 2.3 million limestone and granite blocks.
Stretches over 21000 kilometers across northern China.
Construction spanned multiple dynasties over more than 2000 years.
It is not actually visible from the Moon with the naked eye
Rice flour was mixed into the mortar to help bind the bricks together.
Carved directly into rose-colored sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans.
Known as the Rose City due to the color of the stone used to carve it.
Featured an advanced water channel and dam system to survive the desert climate.
Rediscovered by Western explorers in 1812 after centuries of obscurity.
Could hold an estimated 50000 to 80000 spectators for games and events.
Had a retractable awning system called the velarium to shade spectators.
Featured a complex network of underground tunnels called the hypogeum.
Was partially damaged over centuries by earthquakes and stone robbers.
The El Castillo pyramid aligns with the sun to cast a serpent shadow at equinox.
Home to one of the largest ball courts in ancient Mesoamerica.
Clapping at the base of El Castillo produces an echo resembling a quetzal bird call.
Was a major political and economic center of the Maya civilization.
Built by the Inca without the use of mortar or wheels.
Sits at an elevation of roughly 2430 meters above sea level.
Was abandoned and largely forgotten before being brought to international attention in 1911.
Includes over 100 separate flights of stone steps.
Built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Took approximately 22 years and over 20000 workers to complete.
The main dome appears to change color depending on the time of day and light.
Constructed primarily of white marble inlaid with semi-precious stones.
Struck by lightning multiple times due to its elevated hilltop position.
Stands atop Corcovado mountain overlooking Rio de Janeiro.
The statue's arms span roughly 28 meters wide.
Took around nine years to construct
The largest religious monument in the world by land area.
Originally built as a Hindu temple before transitioning to Buddhist use.
Depicted on the national flag of Cambodia.
Surrounded by a moat over 5 kilometers in perimeter.
Some of its bluestones were transported over 200 kilometers from Wales.
Aligned with the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice.
Construction is believed to have occurred in several stages over 1500 years.
The exact purpose of the monument remains debated among archaeologists.
Served as a cathedral
Its massive dome was an engineering marvel for its era.
Commissioned by the Byzantine Emperor Justinian I.
Contains a mix of Christian mosaics and Islamic calligraphy panels.
Nearly 900 monolithic statues were carved from volcanic rock.
Some statues weigh more than 80 tons.
Most face inland
Believed to represent deified ancestors of the Rapa Nui people.
